newsitem.title: USA: Kantor defends U.S. Commerce in China tools probe.
newsitem.headline: Kantor defends U.S. Commerce in China tools probe.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor Wednesday defended his department's handling of a $1.6 billion aircraft deal in which machine tools sold to China by McDonnell Douglas Corp may have been improperly diverted for military uses.

"The Bureau of Export Administration has done a commendable and appropriate job in making sure not only that they're careful in terms of their approval of licenses for dual-use technology but in following up and making sure it's used appropriately," Kantor said at a news conference. The agency is in his department.
The New York Times reported that a federal grand jury is investigating whether McDonnell Douglas or the procurement arm of the Chinese Aviation Ministry knowingly violated U.S. export control laws.
The agency approved the necessary export licenses for the deal that involved the sale of 40 airplanes, half built in California and half in Shanghai.
A side agreement called for McDonnell Douglas to sell China machine tools for a new machinery plant in Beijing to help build the aircraft.
However, the newspaper reported that the plant was never built and some machinery was diverted to a military factory that produces missiles, violating the terms of the export license.
"You can't warrant in every case there will never be a situation where some country or some entity doesn't try to take unfair advantage of the situation," Kantor said.
But he added, "I'm not speaking directly to this. I don't think it would be appropriate for me to do so."
Kantor also rejected claims levied by some Republicans that Commerce Department trade missions were used to raise campaign funds.
"The principals chosen (to go on trade missions) had nothing to do with politics and everything to do with the economy," he said.
